title: What is known about 1RB1LD_0RC1RC_1RD0RE_0LA0LF_0RF---_1RA1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_0RC1RC_1RD0RE_0LA0LF_0RF---_1RA1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine's two bulk phases are proved in Lean for every length (growth_phase, stall_phase in lean/Phase.lean): they cannot halt. What is left is the short zone at the left end of the tape, which the head rewrites at the end of every phase; it is the only place a halt could happen, and its rule (as a function of the residue of the tape length) has not been worked out. Direct simulation follows 32 phases (1.5·1010 steps, length 104,205) without a halt.
A closed-set search with all remainders of the length allowed (13 November) found no halting class but did not close: the zone is not a finite engine.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 30,881 cells have been visited and 21,505 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.048). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.47).

claims.title: Two sweeps of the growth phase
claims.text: L (110)^(n+4) (111)^j 1 1 0 0 1 A> 0^∞ reaches L (110)^n (111)^(j+6) 1 1 0 0 1 A> 0^∞ in 32j+186 steps, for all n, j and any tape L: two sweeps eat four 110-units at the front and leave 18 ones; the tape grows by 6 cells.

claims.title: Two sweeps of the stall phase
claims.text: L (110)^(n+4) (111)^j 1 1 0 1 1 1 D> 0^∞ reaches L (110)^n (111)^(j+4) 1 1 0 1 1 1 D> 0^∞ in 32j+124 steps: four units become twelve ones, the tape does not grow.

claims.title: Whole phases, by induction
claims.text: For every i, 4i units are eaten in 2i sweeps of either phase without a halt, whatever the zone L holds.

claims.title: Rounds: growth then stall, length × about 3/2
claims.text: In a direct C simulation to 1.5·10<sup>10</sup> steps the run is a strict alternation of growth phases and stall phases (32 phases); at the start of each round the tape is a zone of under 50 cells followed by (110)<sup>k</sup>, and the length goes 252, 372, 546, 817, 1221, 1824, 2731, 4087, 6114, 9162, 13727, 20592, 30881, 46319, 69474, 104203 at the stall-phase starts: L′ = 3L/2 minus a few cells taken by the zone.

claims.title: Accelerated run
claims.text: The macro simulator with unproved linear-cycle jumps (py/fastsim.py) follows the run to about 6·1015 steps (tape length 7·107) with no halt; its lengths agree with the direct run where both exist.

claims.title: No remainder class halts (sampled)
claims.text: From the start of a growth phase, 0<sup>∞</sup> Z (110)<sup>n</sup> 01 A>, the next zone and length depend on the zone Z and on n mod 8, with n' = (3n + k)/2. Following every residue from 1,513 zones, the C simulator found no halt. The set of zones did not close: zones contain inner segments (110)<sup>k</sup> that are rescaled every round, so they grow without bound once all residues are allowed.

claims.title: The zone and the halting question
claims.text: A halt needs the right-moving zigzag (states A, B, C, E, F) to find 1 1 where the 3-periodic tape has its 0; in the body the proved rules exclude it. The zone at the left end (a few walls such as 1110 and runs of ones, rewritten at each phase end, depending on how the front arrives, i.e. on the residue of the length) is not decoded, so whether it can ever present that pattern is open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: Growth and stall phases proved in Lean for every length.
Tape length per round (growth then stall), 32 phases simulated.
Steps simulated directly, no halt (6·10<sup>15</sup> accelerated).

sections.heading: A tape of 110s, a front, and a zone
html: Almost all of the tape is the word 110 repeated. The head works as a bouncer: a front starts at the right end and moves left; on every sweep the head runs from the front to the right end and back. Going right it walks in a zigzag (states A, B, C, E, F, 13 steps per 3 cells), going left it runs fast (A, D, F turn 111 into 101). At the front it eats the last 110 units of the untouched block and leaves ones behind.

There are two kinds of phase, and the run alternates them strictly:

  • growth: two sweeps eat four units (12 cells) and leave 18 ones; each sweep adds 3 cells at the right end;
  • stall: two sweeps eat four units and leave 12 ones; the right end does not move.

When the front reaches the left end it runs into the zone: a few dozen cells holding phase defects (walls such as 1110, runs of ones). The head rewrites the zone, a pass turns the ones back into 110 units, and the next phase starts from the right end. A growth phase turns a tape of k units into about 1.5k units; the stall phase keeps the length. So a round multiplies the length by about 3/2 and costs a number of steps proportional to the square of the length: the right side grows like the square root of the step count, and the zone, which moves left by one or two cells per round, like its logarithm.

sections.heading: Two sweeps, proved for every length
html:
Written with L the zone (any tape), the rules proved in Lean are

growth:  L (110)^(n+4) (111)^j 11 001 A> 0^∞   →  L (110)^n (111)^(j+6) 11 001 A> 0^∞    (32j+186 steps)
stall:   L (110)^(n+4) (111)^j 11 0111 D> 0^∞  →  L (110)^n (111)^(j+4) 11 0111 D> 0^∞   (32j+124 steps)

and by induction on the sweeps, growth_phase and stall_phase: any number of units is eaten without a halt. In the growth phase the count of ones after the front goes 2, 20, 38, … (18 per two sweeps); in the stall phase 14, 26, 38, … (12 per two sweeps).

sections.heading: Only the zone could stop it
html: The machine stops only in state E reading a 1, that is when the right-moving zigzag, coming out of C on a 1, finds a second 1 right after it. In the 3-periodic body the cell after is always the 0 of a 110, which is what the proved phase rules say. So a halt can only come from the zone. The zone changes in a way that depends on how the front arrives, which depends on the residue of the tape length: the same zone word has been seen to lead to different successors (for instance 1110 (110)^5 1110 at lengths 371 and 69,473). This is the shape of a Collatz-like problem, but its rule has not been extracted, so the question is open and no heuristic estimate is given yet.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.048). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.47).
After 109 steps the tape spans 30,881 cells (44 left of the start, 20,547 right), with a density of 1s of 0.696.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A bouncer on a tape of 110-units: each round, a growth phase turns every four units into six and a stall phase re-reads the tape, so the length grows by about 3/2 per round, while a short zone of defects at the left end is rewritten; the zone's rule is not decoded.
